cars.generation: Original RS Cosworth road homologation family
cars.variant: RS Cosworth — August 1992 France road reference
cars.specification_market: Original Ford France August 1992 brochure, nine scanned PDF pages. PDF pages 2, 6 and 7 (printed 2–3, 12–14) visually reviewed for common Motorsport/Luxe road hardware. Motorsport is a road trim, not a competition conversion. Luxe convenience equipment is separate. Native 227 ch DIN at 6250 rpm and 290 Nm at 3500 rpm retained; no UK hp conversion or later small-turbo figures. Exact cc and gearbox not specified on the reviewed pages are omitted. No current fastest/world-first/downforce-number claim.
cars.summary: The Escort RS Cosworth combined a compact Escort-shaped body with extensively developed Sierra-derived turbocharged four-wheel-drive engineering and distinctive front and rear aerodynamic equipment. Created as the basis of Ford’s Group A rally programme while also developed for normal road use, it is a defining road homologation icon of the 1990s.

cars.generation: Original Mk I RS2600 fuel-injected road coupe
cars.specification_market: Original Ford Capri RS German handbook scan, technical-data leaf. Effective displacement 2637 cc is separate from tax displacement 2615 cc. Native 150 PS at 5800 rpm and 22.8 mkp at 3500 rpm retained without conversion. Handbook scan has no securely established edition date: 1970 is the model family introduction, not authentication of this exact handbook revision. Compression, curb weight, performance and brake revisions are omitted. Accessory/competition parts shown on adjacent leaves are not standard-road equipment.
cars.summary: The Capri RS2600 brought the first Capri’s motorsport development into a usable four-seat road coupe. Its fuel-injected V6 and purpose-tuned suspension made the RS concept a coherent engine-and-chassis package, establishing an important European performance-coupe reference rather than a cosmetic sporting edition.

cars.generation: Mk I original RS1600 BDA road family
cars.variant: RS1600 — original October 1970 base recognition reference
cars.specification_market: Original Ford/RAC base form 1605, list 1970/10, printed recognition valid October 1, 1970. PDF pages 1 and 8–11 visually reviewed. Base standard-car engine/drivetrain and manufacturer catalogue declarations only; later competition options, Group 2 evolutions, 2.0-litre engines, RS1800 amendments and 2011 updates excluded. Native 122 BHP at 6500 rpm and 112 lb-ft at 4000 rpm are expressly the form’s notation, not relabelled DIN/SAE, converted kW or silently reconciled with later 115-PS/120-hp summaries. No standard LSD claim.
cars.summary: The Mk I RS1600 established the Cosworth BDA-powered branch of Ford’s Escort performance lineage. Its compact rear-drive road-car basis enabled a remarkably successful rally programme, including the RS1600’s 1973 World Championship breakthrough, making the original sixteen-valve Escort a central performance and rally-history icon.

cars.generation: Mk II original RS1800 BDA road family
cars.variant: RS1800 — October 1975 UK standard road reference
cars.specification_market: Ford Rallye Sport Marketing FP326, October 1975, outer foldout: only the centre RS1800 column is used. Left-column RS2000 1993-cc OHC, 110-PS power, suspension geometry, brake sizes and carburettor details do not apply to RS1800. The leaflet explicitly describes road development and distinguishes RS1800 from RS1800 Custom. Exact displacement, engine torque, top speed and later competition gearbox/tunes are omitted. Not a dedicated rally-car record.
cars.summary: The Mk II RS1800 continued the BDA Escort formula in a distinct second-generation road saloon. Ford’s original sales literature explicitly developed it as a road version of its rally-winning Escort, combining an aluminium sixteen-valve engine with a heavy-duty body and four-speed gearbox; the related competition programme became a World Championship benchmark.
